title: Telemetry-fusion rollback scoring for staged model updates
creator: Ethan Marshall
description: Add a telemetry-fusion based rollback scoring mechanism to the rollout controller so staged model updates (canaries, A/B slices, and shadow traffic) can be automatically and predictively reverted when multiple compatibility signals indicate elevated risk. The goal is a single actionable rollback score that aggregates schema diffs, function-call argument distribution drift, token-level quality regressions, and user-facing error surface signals.
motivation: Current rollout guards are siloed: schema validators fire, function-call diffs log but don't drive a unified decision, and ops often wait for manual review. That leads to slow responses for regressions that are subtle across multiple signals. We need an aggregated, interpretable score that surfaces early multi-signal regressions and drives auto-rollback with configurable hysteresis for production safety.
proposal:
- Instrument the rollout controller to compute a composite rollback score every minute for each variant. The score is a weighted sum of normalized signal sub-scores: schema_conformance, fn_arg_divergence, output_quality_shift, and customer_error_delta.
- schema_conformance uses shape-aware diffing (required/optional fields, type migrations, enum changes) with severity weighting.
- fn_arg_divergence computes Jensen-Shannon divergence over argument distributions and flags new/unseen parameter patterns.
- output_quality_shift compares rolling perplexity/sampling statistics on synthetic prompt subsets and real traffic prefixes; we also include hallucination heuristics for tool-calls.
- customer_error_delta measures increase in user-visible errors (API 4xx/5xx, function-call failures, structured-output parse errors) normalized by baseline traffic.
- Build a small ML calibrator (logistic regression) to map the fused signals to probability of customer-impacting regression using historical rollout incidents as training data. The calibrator runs in the control plane and provides interpretability: feature weights and per-signal contribution.
- Expose scoring and contributing signals in the Console rollout timeline and in the rollout API. Allow per-organization policy overrides and thresholds (auto-revert threshold, probation window, minimum sample size).
rollout_plan:
1) Data collection (1 sprint): add telemetry hooks for argument histograms, schema delta exporter, and synthetic prompt runner. Create a small event schema for exported signals to the rollout engine.
2) Offline calibrator (2 sprints): assemble incident dataset, train logistic regression, evaluate precision/recall at candidate thresholds. Produce conservative default thresholds.
3) Runtime integration (1 sprint): wire scoring into rollout controller with mock mode (score computed but action not taken). Ship Console UI to surface scores.
4) Gradual enablement (2-3 weeks): enable auto-revert for low-risk tenants in Canary mode (5% traffic) with long probation windows; run A/B experiments comparing manual vs. auto-revert decisions.
5) Full enablement and hardening (1 sprint): tighten sampling, add hysteresis, add audit logs and opt-out controls for dedicated/private customers.
metrics: True positive rollback detection rate (compared to postmortem-labeled incidents)
Mean time to rollback after regression detected (minutes)
Customer error increase window (30m/1h) after auto-revert
Rollout score precision/recall at default threshold
Sample size coverage for each variant (min requests/minute)
acceptance_criteria: Scoring pipeline computes a score for every staged variant with <= 60s latency from data availability
Calibrator explains top-3 contributing signals for any score >= auto-revert threshold
In synthetic replay tests of known historical incidents, score would have triggered a rollback within the same window in >= 90% of cases
Auto-revert can be toggled per-org and emits an auditable event (who/when/reason)
Console surfaces the rollback score and a breakdown of contributing signals in the rollout timeline
No more than 1 false-positive auto-revert per 1000 rollouts in initial pilot tenants

infra: design event schema and storage for per-variant signals
ml: assemble incident dataset and train logistic regression calibrator

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: calibration overfits to historical incidents and misses novel regressions. Mitigation: keep a human-in-loop probation window and require minimum sample sizes before auto-revert.
Risk: noisy per-signal metrics cause oscillation around threshold. Mitigation: add hysteresis with separate escalate and de-escalate thresholds and smoothing over 3-minute windows.
Risk: privacy exposure from argument histograms. Mitigation: store k-anonymized histograms and strip PII fields before exporting; consult security team.
Risk: tenants with low traffic will never reach sample size. Mitigation: disallow auto-revert below configurable minimum requests/minute and expose advisory scores only.
Risk: unintended interaction with current rollback/playbook logic. Mitigation: run in audit/mock mode for 2 weeks and add integration tests that assert playbook precedence rules.
